cards.details: Rise of Chandragupta I; adoption of 'Maharajadhiraja' title signaling imperial transition.
Samudragupta and Chandragupta II consolidate power through military conquest and matrimonial alliances.
Increasing grant of land (Agraharas) leads to feudalization and administrative decentralization.

traps.title: UPSC Exam Traps
items: Mistaking Gupta administration as highly centralized; in reality, it was more decentralized compared to the Mauryas.
Assuming 'Vishayapati' were hereditary; they were often appointed by the Provincial Governor (Uparika).
Confusing 'Agraharas' (land grants to Brahmins) with 'Devagraharas' (grants to temples).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geographic Divisions

  • Bhukti: Provinces governed by Uparikas.
  • Vishaya: Districts governed by Vishayapatis.
  • Vithi: Sub-divisions of Vishaya.

Key Officials

  • Kumaramatyas: High-ranking administrative officers.
  • Sandhivigrahika: Minister of Peace and War.
  • Mahabaladhikrita: Commander-in-chief.

Hierarchy of Administration

  • Central Level: King as the source of authority. Council of Ministers (Mantriparishad) provided advice.
  • Provincial Level (Bhukti): Headed by Uparikas, often princes or high officials.
  • District Level (Vishaya): Managed by Vishayapatis assisted by local municipal bodies (Vishaya-mahattaras).
  • Village Level (Gramika): The basic unit of administration, overseen by Gramika assisted by village elders.
